title: 1997 Miami Dolphins season
summary:
The document provides an overview of the 1997 Miami Dolphins season, which was the franchise's 32nd season in the NFL, their eighth under general manager Eddie Jones, and their second under head coach Jimmy Johnson. The main points covered include:

- **Season performance**: The Dolphins improved on their previous 8–8 record by winning nine games, with seven of their sixteen games decided by a field goal or less.

- **New branding**: This season marked the introduction of a new logo and uniforms featuring darker aqua and dark navy drop shadow numbers, which remained in use until the 2012 season.

- **Notable losses**: The Dolphins were defeated by the defending Super Bowl champion Green Bay Packers in Week 3 for the first time in franchise history, and were swept by the New England Patriots, who beat them three times during the season.

- **Playoff appearance**: This was the first of five consecutive playoff appearances for the Dolphins. However, their postseason ended with a 17–3 Wild Card loss to the Patriots, during which Dan Marino threw three interceptions returned for touchdowns by New England across the season.

- **Division title loss**: The Dolphins lost to the Patriots 14–12 on Monday Night Football in Miami just a week before the Wild Card game, costing them the AFC East division title.

- **Other milestones**: This season was the last time until 2021 that the Dolphins swept the New York Jets in back-to-back seasons.

The document also contains sections covering the offseason and NFL draft, team staff, roster, schedule, playoffs, game summaries (beginning with Week 1 against the Indianapolis Colts), standings, and references.
